citeAs: Kunchang Li, Yali Wang, Yinan He, Yizhuo Li, Yi Wang, Yi Liu, Zun Wang, Jilan Xu, Guo Chen, Ping Luo, Limin Wang, Yu Qiao (2024). MVBench: A Comprehensive Multi-modal Video Understanding Benchmark. CVPR 2024.
creator: Kunchang Li, Yali Wang, Yinan He, Yizhuo Li, Yi Wang, Yi Liu, Zun Wang, Jilan Xu, Guo Chen, Ping Luo, Limin Wang, Yu Qiao (Shanghai AI Laboratory, Shenzhen Institute of Advanced Technology Chinese Academy of Sciences, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, The University of Hong Kong, Fudan University, Nanjing University)
description: MVBench is a comprehensive Multi-modal Video understanding Benchmark covering 20 challenging video tasks that cannot be effectively solved with a single frame. It uses a novel static-to-dynamic method to define temporal-related tasks, and automatically converts public video annotations into multiple-choice QA to evaluate temporal understanding capabilities of Multi-modal Large Language Models (MLLMs). The benchmark covers a wide range of temporal skills from perception to cognition, drawing from 11 public video datasets.
name: MVBench
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Automated pipeline using ChatGPT (OpenAI) for QA generation; no human annotation platform mentioned.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: An automatic QA generation paradigm was used to convert open-sourced video annotations into multiple-choice QAs. Two approaches were used: (1) Template-Based Construction: option candidates were constructed directly from ground truth annotations (e.g., for Action Antonym: correct action + opposite action + "not sure"; for Moving Direction: four directions + stationary state); (2) LLM-Based Generation: ChatGPT was used to generate questions based on task definitions and to convert open-ended QAs into multiple-choice format with answer options. For tasks requiring question generation, ChatGPT generated 3 to 5 questions based on task definitions. 200 multiple-choice QA pairs were produced for each of the 20 temporal understanding tasks.
rai:dataBiases: The paper acknowledges a minimal source gap between the instruction data used for VideoChat2 and MVBench: CLEVRER in the instruction data has similar questions as Moving Attribute and Counterfactual Inference tasks in MVBench, and videos for Action Antonym are from SthSthV2 while the antonym labels are from PAXION. The benchmark uses multiple-choice format instead of open-ended answers specifically to avoid biased scoring by LLMs. Ground-truth video annotations from public benchmarks are used to guarantee evaluation fairness and accuracy.
rai:dataCollection: Videos were collected from 11 existing public video benchmarks: STAR, PAXION, Moments in Time V1 (MiT V1), FunQA, CLEVRER, Perception Test, Charades-STA, MoVQA, NTU RGB+D, VLN-CE, and TVQA. Videos were carefully filtered for diversity, temporal sensitivity (primarily 5s to 35s duration), and question difficulty. Multiple-choice QA pairs were automatically generated from the public annotations using LLMs (ChatGPT), producing 200 QA pairs per temporal task (4,000 total across 20 tasks).
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Videos and annotations from 11 public video datasets: STAR (real-world indoor third-person), PAXION (real-world and simulated, indoor and outdoor), Moments in Time V1 (real-world and simulated, indoor and outdoor), FunQA (real-world, indoor and outdoor), CLEVRER (simulated, indoor), Perception Test (real-world, indoor, first and third-person), Charades-STA (real-world, indoor, third-person), MoVQA (real-world, indoor and outdoor), NTU RGB+D (real-world, indoor, third-person), VLN-CE (simulated, indoor, first-person), and TVQA (real-world, indoor and outdoor, third-person).
rai:dataLimitations: Current MLLMs struggle with position, count, and character tasks in MVBench. The benchmark reveals that existing MLLMs have difficulty generalizing to localization and counting tasks without related tuning data. Visual information alone may not be sufficient for cognition tasks like egocentric navigation and episodic reasoning, suggesting that other modalities (depth, audio) could be beneficial. There is a minimal source overlap between the instruction tuning data and MVBench evaluation data (CLEVRER and SthSthV2).
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For STAR dataset clips, start or end points were randomly shifted to increase the complexity of localizing specific events. For CLEVRER, questions requiring more than a specified number of conditions were excluded. Answer options were randomly sampled (3 to 5 per question) from available candidates and shuffled to strengthen evaluation robustness. LLM was used to ensure all answer options have similar and reasonable text lengths to prevent answer leakage from option length differences.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data filtration was applied across three criteria: (1) Video Diversity: selection from 11 video datasets covering broad domains and scenes; (2) Temporal Sensitivity: elimination of short clips with negligible motions and extremely long videos, selecting videos with intermediate duration primarily ranging from 5s to 35s; (3) Question Difficulty: for STAR, video clips were randomly shifted at start or end points to increase complexity; for CLEVRER, questions requiring more than 10 conditions were excluded to decrease difficulty. Answer options were randomly sampled (3 to 5 options) and shuffled. LLM was used to ensure all answer options have similar and reasonable text lengths.
rai:dataSocialImpact: MVBench aims to advance the evaluation of temporal understanding in Multi-modal Large Language Models, which is critical for understanding procedural activities in the real world. By providing a comprehensive benchmark for video temporal understanding, it helps identify gaps in current AI systems and guides the development of more robust video MLLMs for open-world understanding.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating the temporal understanding capabilities of Multi-modal Large Language Models (MLLMs) on video tasks. The benchmark is intended to comprehensively assess temporal perception and cognition skills of MLLMs across 20 challenging video tasks, ranging from action recognition and prediction to episodic reasoning and counterfactual inference. It serves as a diagnostic tool to identify weaknesses in current MLLMs for temporal video understanding.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: ChatGPT was used to generate questions for each video based on task definitions, convert open-ended QAs into multiple-choice format, and ensure answer options have similar and reasonable text lengths. UMT-L/16 model was used to generate top-6 action predictions as answer candidates for the Fine-grained Action task.
